records.name: MANOR HOUSE
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY CHURCH LANE

13/73 Manor House 04/02/69 (Formerly listed as Evenly Manor)

GV II

House. Mid C17. Squared uncoursed limestone and ironstone, ironstone dressings, artificial stone slate roof, brick stacks. T-plan. 2 storeys and attic; 3 bays. Symmetrical front with central gabled porch of 2 storeys. Stone doorway with 4-centred head and square hood. Original studded plank door flanked by 4-light stone mullioned windows with square hoods. Similar windows on first floor, except that above porch with 3 lights. Gabled dormers with wooden casements. Gabled 4-storey wing at rear has C17 five-light window with wood lintel, moulded wooden mullions and iron casemnts. Interior: C17 stone fireplace with 4-centred arch in ground floor room. 2 small straight-headed stone fireplaces, also C17 in bedrooms. Staircase C20 but probably in original central position.

Listing NGR: SP5869034953

records.name: 3, THE GREEN
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (North side) 13/75 No.3 04/02/69

GV II

House. Datestone 1790. Squared uncoursed limestone, slate roof, brick stacks. 2 storeys and attic, 3 bays. Central doorway with wood lintel, 6- panel door, part glazed, and C20 timber and slate hood, flanked by windows with wood lintels and C20 four-light casements. Similar 2- and 3-light windows on first floor, and 2-light in attic. Datestone TH/1790 above central window on first floor.

Listing NGR: SP5865534854

records.name: 4, THE GREEN
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (North side) 13/76 No.4 04/02/69

GV II

House. C18, altered mid C19. Uncoursed limestone rubble, tile roof. 2 storeys and attic. Central doorway with wood lintel and 4-panel door, flanked by windows with wood lintels and C20 two-light wood casements. Gabled dormers with similar casements. Roof tiles laid in bands of blue and yellow. Extension to left C18/C19, 2 storeys, one bay, squared uncoursed limestone slate roof and 2-light casement windows.

Listing NGR: SP5866434871

records.name: 14-21, THE GREEN
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (North side) 13/78 Nos.14 to 21 (consecutive) 04/02/69

GV II

Terrace of 8 cottages. Late C18, altered C19 and C20. Uncoursed limestone rubble, tile roof, brick stacks. 2 storeys, 9 bays. All doorways C20. All windows C20 with wood or concrete lintels. Roof tiles laid in bands of blue and yellow. Included for group value. Remodelled as part of the planned development of The Green in the Cl9.

Listing NGR: SP5873034893

records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (North side) 13/79 No.22 04/02/69

GV II

Listing NGR: SP5873834887

records.name: BORTONS CLOSE
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (North side) 13/80 No.24 (Bortons Close) 04/02/69

GV II

Cottage C17/18. Limestone rubble and squared uncoursed stone. Thatched roof. Brick and stone stacks. 2 storeys and attic, 4 bays. Doorway in second bay from left has wood lintel. Overlight C20 door and C20 stone porch. Wood lintel of blocked window in left bay and below it a cellar window with wood lintel and C20 metal casement and in right bay a window with original stop chamfered lintel. To left of doorway at mezzanine level is 2-light case- ment window with wood lintel. C20 casement windows on first floor. Interior: original newel staircase in thickness of wall left of entrance. Part of raised cruck construction exposed but most roof timbers re-newed. Remodelled 1984.

Listing NGR: SP5876334880

SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (South side) 13/84 No.52 04/02/69 (Formerly listed as Nos.52 and 53)

records.name: THE RED LION PUBLIC HOUSE
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (South side) 13/86 The Red Lion Public House 04/02/69 (Formerly listed as The Red Lion Inn)

GV II

Public House. C18, remodelled c.1850. Squared uncoursed limestone, artificial stone slate roof, stone stacks. 2 storeys and attic, 3 bays. Central doorway with moulded stone lintel and C20 plank door, flanked by bay window with stone mullions. First floor windows have heavy moulded wood casements of 2 lights with plain stone frames. Gabled dormers with similar casements. All windows have octagonal leaded panes. Large double chimney stack with moulded bases and caps. C18 gabled wing at rear.

records.name: THE BOTHY THE PATCH
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY BOUGHTON TERRACE

13/69 No.1 (The Bothy) and No.2 04/02/69 (The Patch) (Formerly listed as No.1 (Errol Cottage) and No.2 (The Patch))

GV II

Pair of Cottages. C17/18. Coursed limestone rubble. Thatched roof brick and stone stacks. 2 storeys and attic, 3 bays. Doorways in second bay from left and second from right have C20 doors and C20 porches. All windows with C20 wooden lintels and 2-light casements. Thatched dormer in left bay also with C20 casement. Interior: No.2 has original newel staircase in the thickness of the wall. No.1, remodelled C20.

records.name: CHURCH OF ST GEORGE
records.details:
SP53NE EVENLEY CHURCH LANE

6/71 Church of St.George

GV II

Church. 1864-5 by Henry Woodyer. Squared coursed limestone, artificial stone slate roof. Wood shingles on spire. In early English stlyle, it consists of chancel, nave and clerestory, aisles, transepts, south porch and west tower with broach spire. Inerior: Elaborate decorative carving. Aisle windows with detached shafts. Original fittings include stone pulpit and font. Marble and alabaster reredes with angel figure. Wall monument to Sir Creswell Levinz, died 1700 attributed to John Nost with over life size marble statue in judges robes and wig. Its architectual background has been removed. Wall monument to H-Glynne Brown died 1803 by R. Blore junior. Relief of mourning woman by an urn. Built for Mrs P.S. Pierrepoint of Evenley Hall as a memorial to her husband. Buildings of England: Northamptonshire.

Listing NGR: SP5842335152

records.name: THE VICARAGE
records.details:
SP53NE EVENLEY BROAD LANE

6/70 The Vicarage

- II

House. c.1830. Limestone ashlar, slate roof. 2 storey. 3 bays with angle pilasters and string course at first floor level. Central porch with fluted Greek Doric columns, engaged pilasters and straight entablature. Doorway has fanlight and side lights. 6-panel door. Sash windows. Hipped roof with wide eaves. 2-storey wing of rendered stone and brick to left.

SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (South side) 13/83 Nos.54 and 55 04/02/69

Two cottages. Mid C19. Squared uncoursed limestone, tiled roof. Stone stack. 2 storeys and attic; 2 bays. Doorways at the sides have wood lintels and plank doors. No.54 has windows with wood lintels and C19 horizontal sashes. No.55 has C20 windows. Roof tiles laid in bands of blue and dark red. Included for group value. Listing NGR: SP5866434782

records.name: 46-49, THE GREEN
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (South side) 13/85 Nos.46 to 49 (consecutive) 04/02/69

GV II

Terrace of 4 houses. Datestone 1877. Uncoursed limestone rubble, brick dressings. Tile roof, brick stacks, 2 storeys. 3 bays. Entrances are recessed between 4 projecting gabled bays, in left and right bay and 2 central bays. Doorways have arched heads and C20 doors. Ground and first floor windows have segment heads and 3-light wood casements. Above each doorway is a one-light casement window. Included for group value. Part of the planned development of The Green in C19.

records.officialName: Chest Tomb Dated 1752 Approximately 4 Metres North of Chancel of Church of St George
records.details:
SP53NE EVENLEY CHURCH LANE

6/72 Chest tomb dated 1752 approx 4 metres north of chancel of Church of St. George

GV II

7hest Tomb. Mid C18. Limestone. Panelled sides with angle balusters. Moulded lid summounted by scrolls and flaming urn. On East face fragmentary inscription. "Robert Pearne, died in Antigua in America in 17..7" On the base "At the bottom of this v..... The body of Will....l..ck. Many years the faithful servant of Robt Pearne." died 1752.

records.name: 2, THE GREEN
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (North side) 13/74 No.2 04/02/69 GV II

House. Datestone 1869. Squared coursed limestone, stone slate roof, stone stack. 2 storeys and attic, 2 bays. Central doorway with wood lintel and 4- panel door, flanked by windows with wood lintel and horizontal sashes. Similar windows on first floor and gabled dormers with horizontal sashes. Datestone above doorway GP/1869. Part of the planned development of The Green in the C19.

Listing NGR: SP5865534844

records.name: DORMER ROW
records.details:
SP5834 EVENLEY THE GREEN (North side) 13/77 Nos.5 to 12 (consecutive) 04/02/69 (Dormer Row) (Formerly listed as Nos.5,6,7, 8,9,10,11 and 12)

GV II

Terrace of 8 houses. c.1869. Squared uncoursed limestone and limestone rubble, tiled roof, brick stacks. 2 storeys and attic, 10 bays. Entrances were originally at rear. Nos.5 to 9 have front doorways inserted C20. Original rear doorways at Nos.ll and 12 with wood lintels and plank doors. All windows have wood lintels. Nos.5 to 9 retain C19 sliding sashes, others have C20 wood casements. Gabled dormer with horizontal sashes or wood casements. Roof tiles laid in bands of blue and yellow. This terrace is said to have been built by the Pierrepoint family of Evenley Hall as part of the development of The Green in the mid C19.

records.name: Evenley War Memorial
records.details:
The memorial stands on the south edge of the large Green. It comprises a simple limestone cross, c4m high, with an inverted sword carved on both the front and rear faces. The shaft rises from a three-stage octagonal plinth on a square base. On the front face of the plinth is inscribed THE GREAT WAR/ 1914-1918/ LEST WE FORGET. The names of the fallen occupy other faces of the plinth. Beneath, on the top tier of the base, is inscribed 1939-1945.

The modern flagged surround to the memorial is excluded from the listing.
